answer: An operator books one numbered ink-loft and receives a sealed sack of tagged walnut hulls plus a uniquely cleaved opal burnishing stone. Only that holder may boil the hulls in that loft's kettle, then burnish a registrar-issued raven quill nib on the opal until the loft's day-book takes a numbered proof stroke. Registrars match hull lot, opal cleavage, quill barb, and kettle log. A shared loft, leftover hulls, or a pre-inked nib is forfeited as one farm. Fielding N aliases costs N exclusive lofts, N unique opals, and N live boils no single inkmaker can run in the same hour.
